assumptions: The edge assumes that browser/UI code execution can produce an unprivileged local OS code-execution context on the host, despite the source description only saying 'potentially execute code'.
The edge assumes Oculus Browser and Oculus Desktop are deployed on the same Windows host; no explicit environment observation establishes this.
The edge assumes the resulting local context can create hard links to OVRRedir.exe log files; the source description does not mention hard links.
The target postcondition's SYSTEM level is inferred from 'gain privileges' and is not stated in the CVE description.

evidence_quotes.quote: via vectors involving a hard link to a log file

missing_conditions: explicit same-host relationship between the Oculus Browser source context and the Windows Oculus Desktop target
source code execution is OS-level unprivileged local user code execution, not merely HTML/UI injection or potential browser code execution
ability to create a hard link to a log file used by OVRRedir.exe from that local context
target host runs Windows with Oculus Desktop before 1.44.0.32849
target local user access/context required by CVE-2020-1885
source version is affected: Oculus Browser 5.2.7 through 5.7.11
target 'gain privileges' maps to the claimed SYSTEM-level privilege escalation
the privileged OVRRedir.exe arbitrary-file-write path is reachable after hard-link setup
response.reason: CVE-2019-3562's actual described effect is that a remote web page can inject arbitrary HTML into Oculus Browser UI, spoof UI, and only 'potentially execute code'; it does not establish OS-level unprivileged local code execution, hard-link creation, or same-host deployment with Oculus Desktop. CVE-2020-1885 requires local users on Windows and a hard link to a log file exploited by a privileged OVRRedir.exe process. The edge bridges from possible browser code execution to an unprivileged local host context; this is a conditional inference, not entailed by the supplied descriptions or explicit environment observations. It cannot enter a strict graph as supported unless those missing same-host, local-execution, and hard-link prerequisites are verified.
